ῥίγιστος.definition: Sup. Adj. formed from most horrible, Il.5.873; A.R.2.215, cf. 292; Nic.Th.64

ῥῖγος.definition: frost, cold, Od.5.472, Hdt.6.44, etc; shivering, Pl.Ti.62b; shivering fit, as in ague, Hp.VM16, Aph.4.29, BGU956.2 ; Hp.Fract.34

ῥίγωσις.definition: shivering, prob. cj. for in Thphr.Vent.23

ῥιζαῖος.definition: forming a base , of a column, opp. Sardis 7 No.181

ῥίζιον.definition: or Dim. of little root, Ar.Av.654, Antiph.45, Thphr.CP2.18.2, HP4.2.3, etc.; vegetable purple , POxy.1051.13

ῥιζοκέφαλος.definition: of plants, of which the flower grows straight from the root, Thphr.CP1.10.5

ῥιζόσημος.definition: with a stripc of vegetable purple , POxy.1051.3

ῥιζοτομέω.definition: cut or prune the roots of a tree by digging; cut up by the roots, extirpate, D.S.32.4: esp. for Medic. purposes, cut and gather their roots, Hp.Ep.16, cf. Thphr.HP4.5.1; gather roots for food, Str.16.4.9: metaph., Phi…

ῥιζοτομία.definition: cutting and gathering of roots, Thphr.HP6.3.2, 9.8.2: pl., books on roots, herbals, Ruf. ap. Orib.7.26.31

ῥιζοτροφέω.definition: grow, nourish roots, Poll.1.235; v.l. for in Str.17.3.23 in Cod. in Sitzb.Heidelb.Akad.1931/2.23

ῥιζοφάγος.definition: eating roots, Arist.HA595a16, PA662b14; Root-eaters, name of an Ethiopian tribe in D.S.3.23, Str.16.4.9

ῥιζόφυλλος.definition: with leaves from the root, Thphr.HP6.4.9, 7.11.3

ῥιζωνυχία.definition: root of the nail, Poll.2.145 , cf. Paul.Aeg.6.85:—in Ruf.Onom.85, but Id. ap. Orib.25.1.32

ῥίζωσις.definition: taking root, Thphr.CP2.12.5, 8.1.3; Plu.Publ.8: metaph., of the formation of the embryo, Philol.13; Plu.Lyc.14; origin of veins and arteries, Hp.Alim.31

ῥικνόομαι.definition: Pass., grow stiff or be shrivelled by; dance with unseemly contortions, S.Fr.316, cf. Luc.Lex.8

ῥιμφάρματος.definition: of a swift chariot, Pi.O.3.37; with the swift racing of chariots, S.OC1063

ῥινεγκαταπηξιγένειος.definition: with a nose reaching to the chin, with a nutcracker nose and chin, Epigr. ap. Hegesand.1

ῥινεγχυτέω.definition: or inject at the nose, ib.179, in Pass

ῥινεγχύτης.definition: instrument for passing such iniections, Cael.Aur.TP 2.4, Aët.6.52

ῥίνη.definition: file, rasp, X.Cyr.6.2.33, Arist.Aud.803a2; shark with a rough skin, used for polishing wood and marble, Rhina squatina, angel fish, Hp.Int.1, Epich.59, Archipp.25, Anaxandr.41.53, Arist.HA540b11, al

ῥινηλασία.definition: tracking by the nose, hunting by scent, Anon. Lond.33.16, Longus1.21

ῥινηλατέω.definition: track by scent, A.Ag.1185, cf. S.Ichn.88, Ph.1.628, Longus2.13

ῥινηλάτης.definition: one who tracks by scent, Poll.2.74

ῥίνησις.definition: filing, of teeth, ib.872; of bones, Id.14.782

ῥινίον.definition: Dim. of I, small file, Gal.12.871; = 2, Cels.6.6.30, Gal.12.736

ῥίνισμα.definition: = I, Ctes.Fr.57.25 , Antyll. ap. Orib.10.19.7, Ruf.Fr.75

ῥινόβατος.definition: a rough-skinned fish, between the species and , perh. Rhinobatus Columnae, Arist.HA566a28; also Id.GA746b6

ῥινοβόλος.definition: striking the nose, of smells, Hsch; proparox. Pass., emitted through the nose, of a snorting sound, AP9.769

ῥινοτορίνιον.definition: dub. in Hermes 38.283 as name of surgical instrument

ῥινοτόρος.definition: hide-piercing, shield- piercing, of Ares, Il.21.392, Hes.Th.934; Nonn.D.45.288, etc

ῥιπίζω.definition: blow up or fan the flame; fan a person, in Med., fan oneself, Hp.VM16:—Pass., Antiph.202.5; to be fanned or blown about, Com.Adesp.1324, cf. Arist.Pr.967a21; Ph.2.511; Ep.Jac.1.6; D.C.70.4: metaph., Alciphr.3.47

ῥίπισις.definition: blowing with a bellows or fan, Thphr.Ign.36 , Gal.8.416, Alex. Aphr.Pr.1.113

ῥίπισμα.definition: air of a fan, etc., AP5.293

ῥιπτασμός.definition: throwing or tossing about, Hp.Acut.54: abs., tossing about in bed, Id.Coac.81, Plu.2.455b; Stoic. 3.100

ῥιπτέω.definition: used only in pres. and impf., collat. form of first in Od., 13.78, where it suits the metre ; so in Ar., Ec.507; Id.V.59; in Trag. is never either guaranteed or disproved by the metre, A.Pr.1043 , S.Aj.239 , Ant.131 ,…

ῥιψασπία.definition: throwing away of the shield, Sch.Hermog.inRh.4.253 W

ῥίψασπις.definition: throwing away one's shield in battle, craven, Ar.Nu.353, Pax1186, Pl.Lg.944b

ῥιψοκίνδυνος.definition: fool-hardy, reckless, X.Mem.1.3.9; Alciphr.1.3; of persons, Id.3.52, Poll.1.179; Ph.1.326, App.BC5.84. Adv. ib.1.103, POxy.2131.16

ῥοδάνη.definition: like spun thread, woof or weft, Batr.183, cf. Eust.1527.60, Sch.Ar.V.1137, etc.; Hsch. gives but

ῥοδανίζω.definition: = Sch. B Il.18.576, cf. Eust.1527.60; Id.1165.22, cf. Heracleon ap.EM702.8, Hsch

ῥοδάριον.definition: Dim. of as an ornament, BGU781 iii 19 ; cj. for in Hsch. s.v

ῥόδεος.definition: of roses, Ibyc.5; like a rose, rosy, AP6.102 ; Nonn.D.9.296

ῥοδεών.definition: rose-bed, BGU1119.11 , Anacreont. App.2.57 p.353 Bgk

ῥοδισμός.definition: ceremony at which graves were decked with roses, Inscr.Perg.374 B 8 , Supp.Epigr.1.330 B8 , BCH24.425

ῥοδίτης.definition: wine flavoured with roses, Dsc.5.27, Gp.8.2 tit

ῥοδοδάκτυλος.definition: Aeol. , rosy- fingered, as epith. of in Hom. and Hes., Od.2.1, Hes.Op.610, etc.; B.18.18; Coluth.99

ῥοδοδάφνη.definition: rose-laurel, i.e. prob. Nerium Oleander, or perh. rhododendron, Dsc.4.81, cf. Plin.HN16.79, Luc.Asin.17, Pseudol.27, Artem.1.77, 2.25

ῥοδοειδής.definition: rose-like, rosy, Musae.114, AP15.40.18 ; f.l. for in Poll.2.70; name of a remedy for nose-bleeding, Orib.Fr.15

ῥοδόμελι.definition: rose-honey, Dsc.5.27, Philagr. ap. Orib.5.17.5, Edict.Diocl.Delph.14, Aët.3.104

ῥοδόπεπλος.definition: with roseate veil or robe, Q.S.3.608

ῥοδόσταγμα.definition: extract of roses prepared with honey, like Sch.Ar.Pl.529; also Paul.Aeg.7.15

ῥοδόστερνος.definition: with rosy breast, epith. of Isis, CIG5115

ῥοδοφόρος.definition: bearing roses, name of Ptolemaïs , LXX3 Ma.7.17 ; dub. sens. in Sammelb.4425 v 6

ῥοδόχροος.definition: contr. rose- coloured, AP5.55 , Dsc.1.111, 2.106, Opp.H.1.130, Anacreont.53.22

ῥοδωνιά.definition: rose-bed, garden of roses, Hecat.37 J; vine with rose-coloured grapes, Phot

ῥόζω.definition: = snarl, of dogs: metaph. of men, Phot., Suid

ῥόθιος.definition: also AP9.32, 10.2; of fishes, guttling, Numen. ap. Ath.7.306d; cf. 2

ῥοθιότης.definition: impetuosity, vehemence, of language, v.l. in Poll.4.22

ῥοίζημα.definition: rushing, whirring noise or motion, as of birds, Ar.Av.1182 , cf. Luc.Musc. Enc.2; Id.JTr.1; of the planetary spheres, Iamb.VP15.65 ; AP5.221

ῥοίζησις.definition: whizzing, hurtling, Theol.Ar.37; shot of an arrow, Aq.Ex. 19.13

ῥομβέω.definition: cause to spin like a whirl, gloss on , Tim.Lex., cf. Hsch. s.v

ῥοπάλιον.definition: Dim. of PPetr.3p.59 , Promathid. ap. Ath.11.489b; part of a Inscr.Délos 442 B 146 ; part of a Roussel Cultes Egyptiens p.217

ῥοπάλωσις.definition: name of a disease of the hair, Id.19.430

ῥόφημα.definition: Ion. that which is supped up, thick gruel or porridge, opp. Hp.Aph.7.68, VM5, Fist.7, Arist.Pr.863b6

ῥόχθος.definition: roaring, of the sea, Lyc.402, 696, 742, Nic.Al.390

ῥύγχος.definition: snout, muzzle, of swine, Stesich.14; Com., of a man's face, Cratin.440, Archipp.1; of a god's face, Arar.1

ῥυζέω.definition: or like growl, snarl, like an angry dog , Hermipp.24 ; also of hawks, Poll.5.89

ῥυηφενής.definition: flowing with riches, abounding, D.P.337, Nonn.D.10.152

ῥυθμίζω.definition: bring into a measure of time or proportion; generally, order, arrange, compose, Arist.Metaph.1075b12, Spir.485b2:—Pass., Id.Ph.245b9

ῥυθμογραφία.definition: noting down of the time or rhythm, CIG3088

ῥυθμογράφος.definition: writing on rhythms, of Hephaestion, Tz. in An.Par.1.95

ῥυθμοποιία.definition: making of time or rhythm, Aristox.Harm.p.34 M., Rhyth.2p.8W., Plu.2.1135c , Aristid.Quint.1.5

ῥυθμόω.definition: shape, Sm.Is.44.12:—Pass. Ion. to be moulded, Democr.197

ῥυΐσκομαι.definition: have diarrhoea, Hld.2.19:—prob. flow; suffer from falling hair, Orib.Eup.4.6

ῥυμβονάω.definition: swing round, Phld.D.3.10; metaph., swing round and throw away, 'to make ducks and drakes' of money, Ael.Fr.146

ῥύμη.definition: force, swing, rush of a body in motion; abs., rush, charge, of soldiers, Th.2.81; of ships, Id.7.70; X.Cyr.7.1.31, cf. Polyaen.4.3.5, al., Ach.Tat.1.12; Ar.Nu.407

ῥυμοτομία.definition: division of a town or camp by streets, Plb.6.31.10, D.S.17.52, Str.14.1.37

ῥυμουλκέω.definition: 2, draw by a line, tow, Lat. remulcare or remulco agere, Plb.1.27.9, cf. Str.5.3.6, D.S.20.74, Peripl.M. Rubr.44, etc

ῥυπαίνω.definition: fut. Isoc.12.63:—Pass; metaph., contaminate, infect, Gal.1.254

ῥυπαρία.definition: dirt, filth, Dsc.1.56 (prob. in 5.74; metaph., sordidness, Critias56 D., Telespp.33, 37 H., Plu.2.60d; D.C.74.5

ῥυπαροκέραμος.definition: of a dirty earthenware colour, Alex.Mynd ap. Ath.9.395e

ῥυπαροφόρος.definition: wearing dirty clothes, Steph.in Hp.2.251 D

ῥυποκόνδυλος.definition: with dirty knuckles, esp. of one who imitates the Laconians, Pl.Com.124, Ar.Fr.718

ῥυποφορέω.definition: wear dirty clothes, Sch.Ar.Av.1554, where Hemsterhuis cj

ῥυπόω.definition: make foul and filthy, befoul :— Pass., to be foul and filthy, Ep.pf. part. Pass., . . Od.6.59, cf. Hp.Mochl.33, Mul.1.66; Sch.Ar.Ach.425; Ph.Fr.9 H.:—Act., dub. l. in Thphr.Char.15.6

ῥύπτω.definition: cleanse, wash, esp. with soap or lye, Id.Mete.359a22; Ti.Locr.100e; Phylotim. ap. Ath.3.79c:—Med., wash oneself, Antiph.148.3, Thphr.HP9.9.3, f.l. in Nic.Al.530; aor. Ph.1.613; Polyaen.8.27: prov., ever since I began …

ῥυσαίνομαι.definition: Pass., to be wrinkled, Nic.Al.78, AP14.103

ῥυσιάζω.definition: Dor. IG42.77.11,al. :—treat as a seize, distrain upon, E.Ion523, cf. SIG629.20 , al., Ph.1.638; of plundering a city as reprisal for stolen property, D.S.8.7:—Pass., to be so treated, A.Supp.424 , E.Ion1406, IGl.c.; r…

ῥυσίδιφρος.definition: preserving the chariot, of a charioteer, Pi.I.2.21

ῥυσίπολις.definition: saving the city, A.Th.129 ; opp. Poet. ap. Hld.3.2

ῥυσότης.definition: wrinkledness, wrinkles, Plu.Galb.13, Antyll. ap. Orib.44.8.2

ῥυσοχίτων.definition: with shrivelled coat or skin, Orph.L.721

ῥυσόω.definition: make wrinkled, shrivel, Dsc.5.92, Hippiatr.11, Sch. Od.13.401:—Pass., to be or become wrinkled, shrivel, Arist.Pr.937a9; of skins hung loosely on opp. Apollod.Poliorc.142.4; of fruits, Dsc.5.6.14, Gp.7.18.3, 10.38.10

ῥύσταγμα.definition: dragging away, maltreatment, in pl., Lyc.1089

ῥυστήρ.definition: rare and late form for; rein, Phot.; cf

ῥυτιδόω.definition: make wrinkled, shrivel up, Arist.Pr.936b10:—Pass., to be wrinkled, Hp.Epid.6.1.13; Arist.HA578a9, cf. GA780a32; Thphr.HP3.10.3; Dsc.1.115; Luc.Luct.16; of bandages, Sor.1.83

ῥυτίδωσις.definition: wrinkling, contraction, e.g. of the eye, Gal.10.171 , Ruf.Fr.78

ῥωγαλέος.definition: broken, cleft, Il.2.417; torn, ragged, Od.17.198; . . 13.435

ῥωγάς.definition: = foreg., ragged, Babr.86; cloven rocks, clefts in the rocks, Theoc.24.95, cf. A.R.4.1448, Nic.Th.389; Posidipp. ap. Ath.8.414e

Ῥωμαΐζω.definition: speak Latin, App.Hann.41, Philostr.VA5.36; hold with Rome, be of the Roman party, App.Pun.68, Mac.7, al

Ῥωμαῖος.definition: a Roman, Plb.10.36.3, etc.; ludi Romani, D.C.37.8

Ῥωμαΐς.definition: fem. of Dam. ap. Suid. s.v

ῥωμαλεόομαι.definition: Pass., to be endued with strength, Arist.Phgn.809a32

ῥωμαλέος.definition: of things, strong, Hdt.3.22; Dsc.1.16 ; robust, virile, AP7.413 . Adv. Gal.6.139, Them.Or.21.249c

ῥώννυμι.definition: Hp.Alim.2; Ti.Locr.103e, Gal.6.581; mostly in pf. Pass. and plpf. :—have strength or might, E.Heracl.636; X.HG3.4.29; so Plu.Publ.23

ῥωπογράφος.definition: one that paints petty subjects , such as still life, like the Dutch masters, EM705.55, perh. to be read in Donat.ad Ter.Eun. 253; cf

ῥωποπωλέω.definition: deal in small wares or frippery, Hsch. s.v

ῥωποπώλης.definition: dealer in petty wares, huckster, LXXNe.3.31 , Gal.12.252, al., prob. in Jahresh.23 Beibl.172 ; written Maiuri Nuova Silloge634

ῥωτακίζω.definition: make overmuch or wrong use of the letter Suid

ῥωχμός.definition: cleft, a runnel or gutter scooped out by heavy rains, Il.23.420, cf. A.R.4.1545, BionFr.1, Opp.C.3.323; Plu.Crass.4; Str.8.5.7

ῥαφανηδόν.definition: Adv. radish-like, of fractures, Erot. s.v. Gal.10.424, Sor.Fract.10; cf

ῥιζόθεν.definition: Adv. = by, from the roots, Id.Al.257, Th.307, Luc.Tyr.13, Q.S.6.381; Supp.Epigr.2.482 :—also Nic.Fr.27

ῥοιζηδά.definition: Adv. with rushing sound or motion, Nic.Al.182,498; also Id.Th.556, Lyc.66, 2 Ep.Pet.3.10, Aesop.30, Aret.CA1.7

ῥύδην.definition: Adv., flowingly, i.e. abundantly, lavishly, Cratin.441, Plu.Sull.21, Caes.29, Luc.39, Eun.VSp.489B., etc.: cf

Ῥωμαϊστί.definition: Adv. in Latin, App.Mith.2, Plu.2.318d, etc

ῥωσκομένως.definition: Adv. pres. part., as if from a Verb = strongly, Hp.Cord.1
